# GapTracks — which gaps each column allows

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean

The smaller of two twin primes above 3 always lies in the 6n-1 column, and the smaller of two cousin primes in the 6n+1 column. In general, a gap starting from the 6n-1 column never leaves remainder 4 on division by 6, and a gap starting from the 6n+1 column never leaves remainder 2; a gap that is a multiple of 6 keeps both primes in the same column. One claim is refuted rather than proved: the number between two primes six apart is not always composite (5, 7, 11 is a counterexample).

## Published sources

Published work this node rests on or relates to; each entry says how.

- [Twin prime (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin_prime) — every twin pair above (3, 5) has the form (6n-1, 6n+1)
- [Cousin prime (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cousin_prime) — cousin primes, the gap-4 case
- [Sexy prime (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexy_prime) — sexy primes, the gap-6 case

## Claims

<a id="twin_prime_mod_six"></a>
### `twin_prime_mod_six`

Twin primes above 3 start in the 6n-1 column.

```lean
/-- **Twin primes start in the 6n-1 column.** -/
def twin_prime_mod_six : Prop :=
  ∀ p : Nat, p.Prime → (p + 2).Prime → 3 < p → p % 6 = 5
```

**Rests on:** [`Wheel6.prime_gt_three_is_candidate`](Wheel6.md#prime_gt_three_is_candidate)

**Proof:** `RNS.GapTracks.twin_prime_mod_six_step` in [`RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="cousin_prime_mod_six"></a>
### `cousin_prime_mod_six`

Cousin primes above 3 start in the 6n+1 column.

```lean
/-- **Cousin primes start in the 6n+1 column.** -/
def cousin_prime_mod_six : Prop :=
  ∀ p : Nat, p.Prime → (p + 4).Prime → 3 < p → p % 6 = 1
```

**Rests on:** [`Wheel6.prime_gt_three_is_candidate`](Wheel6.md#prime_gt_three_is_candidate)

**Proof:** `RNS.GapTracks.cousin_prime_mod_six_step` in [`RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="sexy_prime_same_track"></a>
### `sexy_prime_same_track`

Adding 6 never changes the column.

```lean
/-- **Adding 6 keeps the column** (true for every number, prime or not). -/
def sexy_prime_same_track : Prop :=
  ∀ p : Nat, p % 6 = (p + 6) % 6
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.GapTracks.sexy_prime_same_track_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean)

<a id="sexy_middle_not_always_blocked"></a>
### `sexy_middle_not_always_blocked`

Refuted: the wheel number between primes six apart is not always composite.

```lean
/-- **Refuted: the middle number is not always composite.** It is false that,
for every pair of primes six apart above 3, the wheel number between them is
composite (5, 7, 11 is a counterexample). -/
def sexy_middle_not_always_blocked : Prop :=
  ¬ (∀ p : Nat, p.Prime → (p + 6).Prime → 3 < p → ¬ (sexy_middle p).Prime)
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.GapTracks.sexy_middle_not_always_blocked_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean)

<a id="prime_gap_forbidden_four_from_six_minus_one"></a>
### `prime_gap_forbidden_four_from_six_minus_one`

From the 6n-1 column, no prime gap leaves remainder 4 on division by 6.

```lean
/-- **From the 6n-1 column, no gap leaves remainder 4.** -/
def prime_gap_forbidden_four_from_six_minus_one : Prop :=
  ∀ p q : Nat, p.Prime → q.Prime → 3 < p → p < q → p % 6 = 5 → (q - p) % 6 ≠ 4
```

**Rests on:** [`Wheel6.prime_gt_three_is_candidate`](Wheel6.md#prime_gt_three_is_candidate)

**Proof:** `RNS.GapTracks.prime_gap_forbidden_four_from_six_minus_one_step` in [`RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="prime_gap_forbidden_two_from_six_plus_one"></a>
### `prime_gap_forbidden_two_from_six_plus_one`

From the 6n+1 column, no prime gap leaves remainder 2 on division by 6.

```lean
/-- **From the 6n+1 column, no gap leaves remainder 2.** -/
def prime_gap_forbidden_two_from_six_plus_one : Prop :=
  ∀ p q : Nat, p.Prime → q.Prime → 3 < p → p < q → p % 6 = 1 → (q - p) % 6 ≠ 2
```

<a id="prime_gap_same_track_of_six_dvd"></a>
### `prime_gap_same_track_of_six_dvd`

A prime gap that is a multiple of 6 keeps both primes in the same column.

```lean
/-- **A gap that is a multiple of 6 keeps both primes in the same column.** -/
def prime_gap_same_track_of_six_dvd : Prop :=
  ∀ p q : Nat, p.Prime → q.Prime → 3 < p → p < q → (q - p) % 6 = 0 → p % 6 = q % 6
```

**Rests on:** [`Wheel6.prime_gt_three_is_candidate`](Wheel6.md#prime_gt_three_is_candidate)

**Proof:** `RNS.GapTracks.prime_gap_same_track_of_six_dvd_step` in [`RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/GapTracks.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)
